Home.faqTitle:
A few things
you might wonder.

first.question: I have never done this before. Is that okay?
first.answer: Absolutely. Every workshop starts with the basics, and your host is there to guide you. Curiosity is the only thing you need to bring.

bring.question: What should I bring?
bring.answer: Just yourself and clothes you do not mind getting a little creative in. Materials, tools, an apron, coffee and tea are all included.

cancel.question: What if my plans change?
cancel.answer: Reply to the studio at least 48 hours before your workshop. We will help you move your request to another available session.

Guide.title:
Made by you.
Kept for years.
Guide.intro: A few simple habits help handmade pieces settle into everyday life. Here is how to look after what you bring home.

ceramics.title: Everyday ceramics
ceramics.intro: Your cup or bowl gets stronger in the kiln, but a little gentleness still goes a long way.
ceramics.imageAlt: A ceramic vessel being shaped by hand
ceramics.one: Let a freshly washed piece dry fully before putting it away.
ceramics.two: Avoid sudden changes from very hot to very cold.
ceramics.three: Follow your host’s glaze-specific advice for food, microwaves and dishwashers.

prints.title: Paper & prints
prints.intro: Paper loves a calm spot, away from moisture and strong direct light.
prints.one: Handle prints with clean, dry hands and support both edges.
prints.two: Choose a frame that keeps the print away from the glass.
prints.three: Display it out of direct sunlight to help preserve the colours.

textiles.title: Thread & textiles
textiles.intro: Small stitches can last a long time with gentle cleaning and thoughtful storage.
textiles.imageAlt: An embroidery hoop and colourful threads
textiles.one: Spot-clean first, and test the thread’s colourfastness before washing.
textiles.two: Avoid scrubbing and wringing; reshape gently while damp.
textiles.three: Store your piece dry, away from prolonged direct light.

Rendering.summary: How does this page change language?
Rendering.url: Default mode: the language is hidden in the URL. No full document reload is needed.

server.description: This page reads translated content from Payload on the server for each request. Choosing another language uses App Router navigation to obtain the matching server output; the visible path stays the same.

static.description: English, Croatian and Arabic versions are generated at build time. Choosing another language navigates to the matching prebuilt route. Its route payload may be fetched if it is not already cached, but the content is not generated from the CMS per request.

client.description: The planner body is loaded with ssr: false and rendered in the browser. All three message catalogs are already available. Changing language updates React context, document language, direction and title locally, preserving your plan without requesting new server output. The initial header, footer and loading shell are still prerendered.
